outcomes: Represent scalar calculations as a directed acyclic graph
Explain reverse-mode adjoints and topological order
Implement and numerically check scalar autodiff

computation-graph.name: Computation graph
computation-graph.definition: A graph whose nodes are values or operations and whose edges record dependencies.
computation-graph.explanation: Evaluating an expression creates values in dependency order. Keeping those dependencies produces a directed acyclic graph that can later be traversed for differentiation. A graph may share one node among several operations, so it is not necessarily a tree. Dynamic graphs are built as ordinary program control flow runs; static systems may construct a graph before data evaluation. The graph is a representation of computation, not a picture required at runtime.

adjoint.name: Adjoint
adjoint.definition: The derivative of a selected scalar output with respect to an intermediate value.
adjoint.explanation: Reverse-mode automatic differentiation associates each reachable value with an adjoint. The selected output starts at one, and operations propagate contributions toward their inputs through local derivatives. If an intermediate influences the output along several paths, those contributions sum in its adjoint. In a neural network, parameter adjoints are the gradients an optimizer uses. The word comes from the transposed linear map used in the reverse calculation.

reverse-mode.name: Reverse-mode automatic differentiation
reverse-mode.definition: A differentiation method that propagates one scalar output’s sensitivity backward through recorded operations.
reverse-mode.explanation: The method runs the original computation forward to obtain values, then visits operations in reverse topological order. One reverse sweep computes derivatives of a scalar output with respect to many inputs, matching the common training case of one loss and many parameters. It differs from symbolic algebra because it executes local derivative rules on actual operations, and from finite differences because it does not perturb every input separately.

sources.title: Automatic Differentiation in Machine Learning: a Survey

checks: x*x+x at x=3 produces value 12 and gradient 7
A tanh chain matches central differences
Repeated backward calls clear reachable gradients
Shared nodes are traversed once but receive every operand contribution
Nonfinite intermediates and overflowing adjoints return errors even with a finite root
limitations: Scalar heap nodes are educational rather than efficient
Rc and RefCell make the engine single-threaded
Only addition, multiplication, and tanh are implemented
